entry: Ran the real session store (store.mjs loadSession, saveSessionAsync, drainSessionStore; store/lifecycle-barriers.mjs bumpSessionGenerationAttempt and markSessionClosedAttempt) and manager/session-lifecycle.mjs createSession on a temp MIXDOG_DATA_DIR. The fence barriers run in a second Node process (this recorder with --child, node --import lib/determinism-preload-other-process.mjs, 120 s deadline). Did not run a turn (the provider throws if asked).
exclusions: no value is normalised; timestamps are the virtual clock (see twin.json clock) in the parent and 1700000000000 in the child process

the OS temp dir (os.tmpdir(), separators as Node produced them) -> <TMP>, in string values at barriers/fence ... messages[*].content and bpNEnvironmentContext only (the stored system prompt). The rest of the prompt (scratch dir name under rec-session-lifecycle, environment facts) is the recording machine's and stays as written
crypto.randomBytes(n) (without a callback) returns the next n values of a running byte counter modulo 256
crypto.randomUUID returns 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<12-digit counter> in call order (client tokens, registration ids, server tokens, daemon session ids, call ids all come from it)
Date.now() is 1700000000000 and performance.now() is 0 for the whole run (revisions are Date.now()*1000, queuedMs is 0)
process.pid is 4242 (process.kill(pid, 0) of it answers alive, as it is this process) and process.ppid is 4241; the recorded cwd is the constant "C:\\recorded\\cwd"

product.comparedAgainst: HEAD and the 60 latest commits touching src/apps
product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: mixdog-core-session close.rs `the_barriers_leave_what_node_recorded` and `a_stale_save_is_refused_as_node_refuses_it` (tests in native/core/crates/mixdog-core-session/src/session/close.rs, which include this twin.json): detach_fields / tombstone / drops_against over the recorded steps. barriers[].steps[].before/after and fence[].recorded are the nine lifecycle keys those tests read; beforeFull/afterFull, late, recordedFull and storedAfter are the whole stored sessions for a replay that drives the store (thread/delete and the close barriers of the Rust SessionDirectory) and compares whole records.
